messages:
claire_sales: Heads-up: AtlasCare wants a 4-week Private POC for their med-qa model (med-qa-7b-v2). Requirements: SentencePiece 32k tokenizer, CMEK (HSM), int4 quant, p50 <150ms single-user. Can infra/security confirm blockers?
ian_se: Tokenizer parity is critical. Ask them to upload .spm + vocab. Small id drift can break clinical prompts.
hugo_infra: I'll run a focused compatibility sweep: tokenizer diff, int4 vs fp16 canary, KV-cache stability, perf for seq=128/512 at conc=1. Will report p50/p95 and perf delta.
sophie_sec: Short SOC/KMS blurb: "Redwood Private supports customer-managed keys (CMEK) with HSM-backed KMS. Customers control key rotation; Redwood does not persist plaintext keys. Audit logs exportable; SOC2 Type II summary available under NDA."
claire_sales: Thanks. Also need a POC quote (infra + 8 eng hours). Can you ballpark int4 vs fp16 cost delta?
hugo_infra: Ballpark: int4 often reduces infra cost ~30-40% vs fp16 depending on kernel maturity. I'll provide refined numbers after the sweep.
bot_oncall: Ticket RINF-12456 created: "AtlasCare med-qa-7b-v2 Private POC compatibility sweep". Assignee: hugo_infra. ETA 72h.
ian_se: I'll prepare a clinical prompt set (abbrs, drug names). If tokenizer mismatch occurs, propose a canonical tokenizer export or fp16 canary.
claire_sales: I'll request their .spm and sample prompts and draft the POC quote including the SOC blurb. Will update the customer after test results. :thumbsup:
